      <title>Controversial vaccine trial touted by RFK Jr gets go-ahead in Guinea-Bissau</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/oct/09/vaccine-trial-guinea-bissau-rfk-jr</link>
      <description><p>Recommended dose of hepatitis B vaccine will be withheld from thousands of newborns by Danish researchers</p><p>A controversial research trial that will withhold hepatitis B vaccines from some African newborns was given approval to move forward this week.</p><p>It is a central part of the vaccine vision for Robert F Kennedy Jr, the secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime vaccine opponent.</p><p>This article was amended on 13 October 2026. A previous version said CIDRAP first reported news that the research trial was approved by the Denmark ethics committee.       <description><p>Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</p><p></p><p>The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/sep/16/israel-committed-genocide-in-gaza-says-un-inquiry">that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza</a>.</p><p>The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/09/navanethem-navi-pillay-wins-nobel-peace-prize">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Isaias strengthens to become first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 season</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/09/isaias-strengthens-first-atlantic-hurricane-2026</link>
      <description><p>Storm expected to make landfall on US’s northern Gulf coast with risk of flash floods and isolated river flooding</p><p>Isaias has become the first Atlantic hurricane of the 2026 season, with wind speeds of 80mph and a minimum pressure of 975mb. It is expected to strengthen to a category 2 hurricane as it approaches the US’s northern Gulf coast on Friday, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).</p><p>As a result of <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/sep/26/what-is-el-nino-causes-can-we-reduce-risks">the strong El Niño</a>, it has been a notably quiet Atlantic hurricane season. The first hurricane of the season has not formed this late since 8 October 1905, which pre-dates the satellite era (1960s) for tracking hurricanes that has allowed for more non-landfall hurricanes to be discovered.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/oct/09/isaias-strengthens-first-atlantic-hurricane-2026">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Matsadaash staff allege torture and forced confessions after being held on charges of working for Muslim Brotherhood</p><p>Egyptian journalists are planning a new protest in Cairo this weekend after <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/04/egyptian-journalist-faces-terrorism-charges-entire-newsroom-detained-matsadaash-press-freedom">six colleagues were charged with terrorism offences</a> amid allegations they had been tortured in police detention.</p><p>Last week, Egyptian authorities arrested the journalists, from the independent factchecking and investigative platform Matsadaash, accusing them in a statement of being unlicensed and producing false news on behalf of the outlawed <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/muslim-brotherhood">Muslim Brotherhood</a>.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/09/egypt-six-journalists-matsadaash-protest-over-detentions">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 22:09:57 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Sport</category><title>Arsenal thrash Lille as Atletico Madrid beat Manchester United</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/sport/20261013-arsenal-thrash-lille-as-atletico-madrid-beat-manchester-united</link><description>
Arsenal scored three goals in seven second-half minutes on Tuesday to beat Lille 3-0 and maintain their perfect Champions League start, while Atletico Madrid defeated Manchester United 2-0 to deepen the pressure on Michael Carrick. Bayern Munich were held to a shock 3-3 draw by Norway’s Viking after Michael Olise was sent off.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b20b7d10-c74a-11f1-9887-77317c09f325/w:1024/p:16x9/ee08db7faf140d19485901258355c8cd6e0a2034.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b20b7d10-c74a-11f1-9887-77317c09f325/w:1024/p:16x9/ee08db7faf140d19485901258355c8cd6e0a2034.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">66808be0-c751-11f1-aac4-3fd31d15ede2</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 21:59:44 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b20b7d10-c74a-11f1-9887-77317c09f325/w:1024/p:16x9/ee08db7faf140d19485901258355c8cd6e0a2034.jpg">© Adrian Dennis, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Pope Leo has cancerous growth removed in lung operation</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/pope-leo-has-cancerous-growth-removed-in-lung-operation</link><description>
Pope Leo XIV had a cancerous growth removed from his right lung in a 90-minute operation on Tuesday and "woke up normally" after the procedure, the Vatican said. A Vatican source said further tests were being carried out to determine if the cancer had spread. "To ensure the procedure was radical, the lower lobe of the right lung was removed," the Vatican said in a statement. FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta reports from Rome.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/16231fa6-c74b-11f1-a4f0-e362370cce2e/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261013-230330-230812-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/16231fa6-c74b-11f1-a4f0-e362370cce2e/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261013-230330-230812-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">1b51ea8e-c74b-11f1-aa5e-db1448cc4d3c</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 21:23:45 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Business</category><title>China is bringing car production to EU</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/business/20261013-china-is-bringing-car-production-to-eu</link><description>
China has moved from exporting cars to bringing entire auto industry ecosystems, building up production capacity in Europe and boosting partnerships with local companies. Arthur D. Little's automotive expert Philipp Seidel tells France 24 that while tariffs and quotas can buy time, EU carmakers must improve their own competitiveness and not become too dependent on Chinese suppliers. But first, we look at the latest IMF global growth forecast and warning about rising debt. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ba4dd768-c748-11f1-b56e-3774aeac812a/w:1024/p:16x9/202610132620CC-FRANCE-MOTOR-SHOWCHINESE-BRANDS.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ba4dd768-c748-11f1-b56e-3774aeac812a/w:1024/p:16x9/202610132620CC-FRANCE-MOTOR-SHOWCHINESE-BRANDS.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5b79815c-c74c-11f1-ab38-eb48f5b06699</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 21:23:38 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Yuka ROYER</dc:creator></item><item><category>A propos</category><title>Supermarket fridge hacking attacks due to lack of basic cybersecurity measures, expert says</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/a-propos/20261013-supermarket-fridge-hacking-attacks-due-to-lack-of-basic-cybersecurity-measures-expert-says</link><description>
French investigators on Tuesday ​were hunting the hackers who seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets in a cyberattack that underlined the vulnerabilities of connected systems, with no group publicly claiming responsibility. <![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Tue, 13 Oct 2026 21:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 13, 1773: Astronomer Charles Messier discovers the Whirlpool Galaxy before we ever knew it was a galaxy ]]>

On Oct. 13, 1773, a French astronomer named Charles Messier discovered the "Whirlpool Galaxy," also known as Messier 51, or M51.

Charles Messier was scanning the sky for objects that could confuse comet hunters when he catalogued the galaxy as M51. However, Messier wasn't able to see the spiral structure, and he didn't identify it as a galaxy.

Seventy-two years later, another astronomer named William Parsons saw the whirlpool shape, but he thought it was a spiral nebula. Eventually, Edwin Hubble found out that M51 and other features like it were actually galaxies.

Why it mattered

The Whirlpool Galaxy is located about 31 million light-years from Earth and just might be the textbook case of a spiral galaxy. But in 1773, it was just one of 51 (at the time of its discovery) of "comet-like 'objects to avoid'" in the night sky.

The Whirlpool Galaxy's designation as M51 marks it as the 51st non-comet object catalogued by Messier, who was the chief astronomer of the Marine Observatory in Paris dedicated to studying comets. According to a NASA account, Messier stumbled across his first non-comet object, M1 (also known as the Crab Nebula), while studying a comet in 1758. The objects looked like fuzzy blobs like comets, but didn't move like a comet. By 1773, at the time he first spotted M51, he had catalogued over four dozen such objects to help prevent astronomers from mistaking them for comets.

The Whirlpool Galaxy appears as a dazzling spiral in images by the Hubble Space Telescope, and has a magnitude of 8.4 on the brightness scale used by astronomers. That means it can be observed through a small telescope ("most easily during May," NASA says) in the constellation Venatici (the Hunting Dogs) in the northern sky, just below the handle of the Big Dipper star pattern.

Scientists suspsect the Whirpool Galaxy gets is striking spiral shape from a close interaction with its neighbor galaxy NGC 5195, which may have passed through M51's main disk about 500 million years ago, scientists with NASA's Spitzer Space Telescope have said.

"This gravitational tug of war may also have triggered an increased level of star formation in M51," they added in a statement. "The companion galaxy's pull would be inducing extra starbirth by compressing gas, jump-starting the process by which stars form."

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'We basically did Top Gun in space': 'Star Trek Starfleet Academy' warps back into action in March 2027 for sophomore year in the final frontier ]]> NEW YORK — Set your phasers to back-to-school, space fans. Star Trek is going back to Starfleet Academy for season 2, and we finally have a release date.

The sophomore season of "Star Trek: Starfleet Academy" will warp back to the small screen in March 2027 when the limited series returns for its final season on Paramount+. The series, which follows a class of cadets balancing Starfleet classes, space adventures (and yes, some love) in the 32nd century, will return with its full cast and even add new faces, showrunners announced at a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 on Saturday (Oct. 10).

"Season one is about letting go of who you were in the past to start again at Starfleet Academy," executive producer and co-showrunner Noga Landau said in the Star Trek panel. "Season two is about thinking that you knew who you were, only to realize that as you grow older, your life is going to go in directions you didn't expect, and you're going to have to shift your perception of yourself. So it's really about sophomore year, right?"

Paramount+ Essential (ads): $5.99 /mo
Paramount+ with SHOWTIME (no ads): $11.99 /mo

Star Trek: Starfleet Academy will be available to watch on Paramount+. You can also watch almost every other Star Trek show and movie on there, too, while you wait.View Deal

Holly Hunter returns as academy chancellor Nahla Ake, a long-lived half-Lanthanite, who will have to face a familiar face in her estranged father, Nyk Ake, portrayed by Bill Nighy (Living, About Time) in season two.

"He plays my full lanthanide father, who has basically, if he wants, can achieve immortality," Hunter said, dropping a big preview about her character in season two. "He plays my dad, and I play me ... and my twin, my twin sister. Very fun."

Also joining this year's Starfleet Academy class is Rosemarie DeWitt (Untamed, The Staircase) as Laytha Sadal, the First Lady of Betazed (and mother of Academy cadet Tarima).

"We have had such a blast," Hunter said of working with the entire cast of Starfleet Academy. "It was a tremendous honor and learning experience for me to do the show for two seasons, and I just really am excited about the second season because there's so much more intimacy that we just comfortably felt with each other over those 10 episodes."

In season one, Starfleet Academy brought back Trek's favorite Emergency Medical Hologram, The Doctor (Robert Picardo), then gave the 800-year-old Star Trek: Voyager physician a daughter in the photonic Sam (Kerrice Brooks) and a Klingon medical student, Jay-Den Kraag (Karim Diané), to train.

We basically did Top Gun in space ..."

showrunner Alex Kurtzman

"His future existence is forever changed. Nothing will ever be the same for the character," Picardo said in the panel. "The shock of that, and how that changed the character, [...] informs all of season two. My primary relationships are now with my daughter and of course with Jay-Den, as I'm mentoring him as a future physician, and we have some terrific scenes together as well."

Executive producer and co-showrunner Alex Kurtzman promised more space action in season two of Starfleet Academy and showed an exclusive teaser clip of Academy cadets Caleb (Sandro Rosta), Genesis (Bella Shepard) and Sam as they race to recover data from a crashed spaceship on their first away mission. But the best, Kurtzman said, is yet to come when the show's cadets meet up with Nova Squadron, the elite flight team at Starfleet Academy.

"The Nova Squadron episode is amazing on a lot of different levels," Kurtzman said. "We basically did Top Gun in space. "What's available to us now technologically allowed us to go to a place that I don't think we've ever gone to on television before. Certainly not in Star Trek."

Star Trek: Starfleet Academy will return to TV in March 2027 on the Paramount+ streaming platform.

Paramount+ Essential (ads): $5.99 /mo
Paramount+ with SHOWTIME (no ads): $11.99 /mo

Star Trek: Starfleet Academy will be available to watch on Paramount+. You can also watch almost every other Star Trek show and movie on there, too, while you wait.View Deal

]]> <![CDATA[ See the original Galileo shuttle from 'Star Trek' in its new home at the Original Series Set Tour in New York ]]> Nostalgia is a hell of a thing, especially when it comes to sci-fi. For "Star Trek" fans wanting to mark the franchise's 60th anniversary this year, a geeky pilgrimage to upstate New York should be on the cards. Why? Because alongside the splendid autumnal colors, they can steer over to Ticonderoga to behold the newly installed Galileo shuttlecraft.

After a complete two-year restoration project in 2012 headed up by superfan and collector Adam Schneider, this iconic fictional spacecraft, seen by millions in seven episodes over three seasons of "Star Trek: The Original Series," was recently relocated from its former home at the Johnson Space Center Museum in Houston, Texas.

It's now on permanent loan to James Cawley and his Star Trek Original Series Set Tour in historic downtown Ticonderoga, New York, where it joins a family of painstakingly detailed sets based on the official "Star Trek" blueprints.

'Galileo is still the property of Space Center, and it was on display there since 2013," Schneider tells Space. "It went to USS Intrepid for the 50th anniversary of 'Star Trek,' displayed under the Enterprise Space Shuttle. ]]> <![CDATA[ Earth's poles shifted surprisingly fast during the age of dinosaurs, ancient sea levels reveal ]]> The location of Earth's geographic poles has changed several times over the past 320 million years in a process known as true polar wander, according to measurements of ancient flooding brought about by sea level changes resulting from our planet's crust shifting relative to Earth's spin axis.

Such a shift can affect climate, both on local scales and globally, as regions that were by the poles find themselves moving down to lower latitudes and vice versa. This can then affect atmospheric circulation patterns, which affect climate across the world.

The changes would have affected the environments in which life developed and evolved, from the age of the dinosaurs through to some of our oldest primate ancestors.

True polar wander is not the same as a change in the rotational axis of the Earth. Currently, Earth spins at an angle of 23.4 degrees relative to the plane of its orbit around the sun, and this rotational axis can vary periodically over tens of thousands of years as a result of the Milankovitch cycles caused by the gravitational pull of the sun and planets.

True polar wander is different. Here, the angle of Earth's spin axis does not change relative to its orbital plane. Instead, Earth's crust and mantle shift relative to that rotational axis. This is because Earth is not perfectly spherical. Instead, it is oblate, with Earth's rotation causing the equator to bulge out and the poles to slightly flatten. Because Earth is not spherical, it has multiple axes of inertia, the largest one being aligned with the rotational axis.

These axes need to be balanced to prevent Earth's rotation from becoming chaotic. However, plate tectonics and indeed the Milankovitch cycles can upset that balance of mass, for example by causing more continental crust to congregate in one hemisphere than another.

To rebalance things, Earth's crust and mantle must become decoupled from our planet's core, which stays aligned with the rotational axis. In physical terms, if there is more continental crust in one hemisphere, the crust and mantle might rotate in that direction relative to the rotational axis and the Earth's core in order to balance itself. This sees the geographical locations of the poles change, hence the name 'true polar wander'.

Currently, true polar wander takes place at a rate of 10 centimeters (4 inches) per year, but figuring out when and how fast true polar wander has occurred in the past is not without its difficulties, not least since plate tectonics can mask and even mimic the signal of true polar wander.

Previous studies relied on paleomagnetism, the study of residual magnetic traces in ancient rocks, since the orientation of those magnetic traces would have varied depending upon where that rock was located relative to Earth's magnetic field. Alas, it's not a terribly accurate means of measuring true polar wander and scientists arrived at substantially different conclusions using this technique.

Nevertheless, based on paleomagnetism, scientists had concluded that true polar wander had been negligible, or slow to proceed, in the distant past. However, new results from researchers at the Centre for Planetary Habitability at the University of Oslo in Norway, led by Mathew Domeier, have shown this not to be the case.

Domeier's team looked through the geological record to track how sea level has changed across millions of years. True polar wander would bring about an identifiable pattern in sea-level changes as the oceans reacted in response to changes in the mass distribution of the planet. The sea level changes would be equal but opposite between hemispheres — sea level rises on one side of one hemisphere would be matched by rises on the other side of the opposite hemisphere, creating a 'quadrupolar' effect.

By using statistical modeling on maps of sea level changes across intervals of 10 million years, Domeier's team identified four periods of true polar wander: in the early Jurassic period 190—200 million years ago, the late Jurassic — early Cretaceous period 140—150 million years ago, during the mid-Cretaceous 90—100 million years ago and from the Oligocene period 30 million years ago through to the Miocene 20 million years ago.

The results show that, contrary to established opinion, true polar wander can happen in bursts that are relatively fast on geological timescales, with the results showing that during the episodes of true polar wander the Earth's surface shifted by as much as 0.6 degrees per million years relative to the spin axis. This is slow by human standards, but fairly fast on geological timescales, certainly quicker than plate tectonics.

Domeier's team were also able to rule out a suspected case of true polar wander around 300 million years ago when the last great supercontinent, Pangea, migrated northwards. It turns out that Pangea's movements were entirely due to plate tectonics.

The findings were published on Oct. 1 in the journal Science.

]]> <![CDATA[ SpaceX rocket launch creates incredible 'space jellyfish' visible throughout US East Coast (photos) ]]> Rockets are launching to space on a near-daily basis these days, but short of livestreaming a liftoff from the comfort of your Wi-Fi router, relatively few spectators are in the right place and time to see one with their own eyes.

That wasn't the case Tuesday morning (Oct. 13), when SpaceX launched the CRS-35 mission for NASA. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Pad 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida at 6:35 a.m. EDT (1035 GMT), carrying a cargo variant of SpaceX's Dragon spacecraft on the company's 35th commercial resupply mission to the International Space Station (ISS). Following the northward path of the space station's orbit at the time, the rocket flew a trajectory along the United States' East Coast.

Falcon 9's expanding engine plume grew substantially wider than the rocket itself as it climbed in altitude into thinner, less dense air, and was illuminated by the early dawn light, making the sight visible to millions. "You can imagine my surprise when I opened my back door to let the dogs out this morning," Ellen Alence told Space.com. She snapped a pic of the rocket from her farm Colbert, Georgia.

"Many of you are talking about the 'space jellyfish' following this morning's launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida," NASA's Kennedy Space Center wrote in a post on X. The post explains the "jellyfish" phenomenon that is sometimes visible during dawn and dusk launches, and included additional photos of the launch.

"A jellyfish happens near sunrise or sunset when the exhaust plume from the rocket becomes brightly illuminated, creating a glowing shape resembling a jellyfish," the post said.

Further up the coast, Richard Mack Wilson-Leigh spotted the flight from Durham, North Carolina. His view of the rocket came just seconds before the vehicle's stage separation, which was followed immediately by the rocket's main booster performing an engine burn to right its trajectory for landing back at the Cape. Wilson-Leigh said that part caught him off guard more than the initial site of the rocket. "I thought it blew up at first," he jokingly told Space.com.

"At first, I thought it was a comet," Wilson-Leigh said. "My mind jumped between two thoughts: that is just beautiful beyond belief, and it is the end of the world.”

That stage separation came about 2.5 minutes after liftoff, and put on a dazzling display for those awake to see it this morning. As Falcon 9's booster began the journey to its landing zone, the rocket's second stage continued onward to orbit with Dragon and the capsule's 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of cargo for the ISS.

The spacecraft will spend roughly two days catching up to the ISS, where a recent personnel rotation swapped the astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission with those of Crew-13. The latter arrived aboard the orbital laboratory Oct. 1, which was followed several days later by the return of Crew-12 to Earth on Oct. 8.

The Dragon carrying the contents of CRS-35's manifest will arrive at the station Thursday morning (Oct. 15), and will autonomously dock to the space-facing port of the Harmony module at around 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT). Coverage of the arrival here at Space.com beginning at 9:15 a.m. EDT (1315 GMT).

The post explains the "jellyfish" phenomenon that is sometimes visible during dawn and dusk launches, and included additional photos of the launch.

"A jellyfish happens near sunrise or sunset when the exhaust plume from the rocket becomes brightly illuminated, creating a glowing shape resembling a jellyfish," the post said.

Further up the coast, Richard Mack Wilson-Leigh spotted the flight from Durham, North Carolina. His view of the rocket came just seconds before the vehicle's stage separation, which was followed immediately by the rocket's main booster performing an engine burn to right its trajectory for landing back at the Cape. Wilson-Leigh said that part caught him off guard more than the initial site of the rocket. "I thought it blew up at first," he jokingly told Space.com.

"At first, I thought it was a comet," Wilson-Leigh said. "My mind jumped between two thoughts: that is just beautiful beyond belief, and it is the end of the world.”

That stage separation came about 2.5 minutes after liftoff, and put on a dazzling display for those awake to see it this morning. As Falcon 9's booster began the journey to its landing zone, the rocket's second stage continued onward to orbit with Dragon and the capsule's 6,300 pounds (2,860 kilograms) of cargo for the ISS.

The spacecraft will spend roughly two days catching up to the ISS, where a recent personnel rotation swapped the astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission with those of Crew-13. The latter arrived aboard the orbital laboratory Oct. 1, which was followed several days later by the return of Crew-12 to Earth on Oct. 8.

The Dragon carrying the contents of CRS-35's manifest will arrive at the station Thursday morning (Oct. 15), and will autonomously dock to the space-facing port of the Harmony module at around 11 a.m. EDT (1500 GMT). Coverage of the arrival here at Space.com beginning at 9:15 a.m. EDT (1315 GMT).

]]> <![CDATA[ 2 spacecraft in orbit and 8 more coming soon: Varda has big plans for in-space manufacturing ]]> Reentry and orbital-manufacturing provider Varda Space Industries is operating two spacecraft in orbit right now, with another expected to launch "in the coming days" and seven more next year.

The Los Angeles-area startup, which bills itself as one of just two companies that can currently do commercial reentry from space, successfully launched its latest two refrigerator-sized spacecraft aboard SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare mission on Oct. 1.

"It's humanity's first time launching multiple commercial reentry vehicles simultaneously," Varda CEO Will Bruey told Space.com on Tuesday (Oct. 7) of the Transporter-18 launch.

The payloads on the Transporter-18 Varda craft ranged from pharmaceuticals to demo navigation systems to exterior thermal-protection materials. The company bills its spacecraft as mini-factories, which can host the orbital production of valuable goods such as pharmaceuticals and then bring them safely down to Earth.

Another Varda vehicle is scheduled to follow them into space later this month. Assuming the third spacecraft launches nominally, all three will come down before Christmas in the Koonibba Test Range in the South Australian Outback, through coordination with Varda's long-time space-mission service provider, Southern Launch. And things are scheduled to ramp up quickly: Varda aims to fly seven more missions in 2027: two in Quarter 1 (Q1), two in Q2 and three in Q3 (the latter three being all on the same rocket).

"As we scale up, we care about our ability to fly and fly regularly," Bruey said, emphasizing that the company is now treating its missions less as one-offs and more as a series. "It is, first and foremost, taking that unique [spacecraft] technology and moving into a fleet mentality, rather than a space mission mentality."

Like any startup finding its footing, Varda's challenges in the coming months will be scaling safely and efficiently. But the company says it is well-capitalized to do so, and has a big hiring campaign underway. It also has been spending money on slight upgrades and improvements to its vehicles, as well as mission operations and other infrastructure to run several missions at the same time, with more funds having just arrived.

In September, Varda announced it had raised $251 million in "Series D" investment funding and will be hiring 100 people by the end of 2027, boosting its current 286-employee base by more than a third. Most of the employees work out of El Segundo, California, with a few in sales offices in Washington, D.C. and Huntsville, Alabama (where U.S. Space Command is gradually moving, along with some defense contractors, from Colorado Springs).

In the further future, Bruey said, the goal is to fly Varda vehicles into space daily, using a "standardized product" that would be put together on an assembly line. But to get to that point, like other companies in the industry, Varda will need to get through an anticipated rocket shortage beginning in about 2029.

SpaceX is by far the most active launcher these days, and it has been the dominant provider for companies like Varda via its Transporter and Bandwagon rideshare programs. But SpaceX is readying to retire its Falcon 9 rocket as it transitions more resources into Starship, the fully reusable megarocket the company sees as its workhorse of the future. Media reports suggest that SpaceX is pretty much out of capacity for Falcon 9 rockets flying through the end of service in 2028 or 2029, although slots are still available through third-party bookers.

There are a slew of newer rockets under production (such as Blue Origin's New Glenn and Relativity Space's Terran R), though they are far less mature and in some cases, even unflown. This is creating uncertainty about how much capacity there will be in the industry in the short term, but Varda said it is planning well ahead for that moment — and so too are its customers.

"We're stacked with launches from now through that 2029 time frame," Bruey said. The company's current generation of vehicles is "launch-agnostic," although the next generation is aiming to be even more so to nab opportunities from small rockets up to Starship.

The company said that, as long as Varda and its customers have access to microgravity, the shipping methodology — much like shipping on Earth — should not matter, and Varda aims to make the experience that seamless for its customers. But in the meantime, the company says it will fly as much as possible and (like everyone else) do what it can to secure slots on launching rockets after Falcon 9 retires.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Space Gal' Emily Calandrelli launches into the Marvel Universe this week on Disney Jr.'s 'Iron Man' series (exclusive) ]]>

"The Space Gal" is blasting off onto her next adventure to promote STEM education with out-of-this-world content.

Science communicator and citizen astronaut Emily Calandrelli, better known to millions of social media followers as "The Space Gal," is bringing her real-world spaceflight experience to the Marvel universe. Calandrelli is lending her voice to an upcoming episode of Disney Jr.'s animated series, "Marvel's Iron Man and his Awesome Friends."

She is stepping into the role of a character called Astronaut Amy in the episode "The Iron Friends in Space," offering another opportunity for Calandrelli to share her enthusiasm for space with younger audiences.

Calandrelli is an engineer, author and television host whose career has focused on making complex scientific concepts engaging and accessible. Growing from her online presence as @TheSpaceGal, Calandrelli has produced numerous educational videos, books and television appearances, including a role on the Netflix "Bill Nye the Science Guy" revival series, "Bill Nye Saves the World."

In a preview clip provided exclusively to Space.com by Disney, Calandrelli's character is welcomed by Tony Stark, Riri Williams, Amadeus Cho and Vision as they explore a moon-themed museum display. The exhibit features a holographic model of the moon and other space-themed artifacts, providing a backdrop for Astronaut Amy to share information about space and lunar exploration.

The show follows younger versions of Stark and others from Marvel's familiar superhero roster, as they navigate conflicts that are scaled down from the franchise's world-ending blockbuster emergencies to more age-appropriate problem-solving and teamwork-building storylines.

Calandrelli's cameo puts her alongside characters already rich in their storylines with backgrounds in science and technology, like Stark and Williams, known by their alter egos Iron Man and Ironheart, both of whose superhero identities revolve around the mastery of sophisticated technology and engineering. And while Astronaut Amy and her super co-stars live in Marvel's fictional universe, Calandrelli's inclusion in the episode creates the opportunity to introduce some real-life scientific concepts.

Her appearance also comes as Disney prepares to expand the animated series to include a larger ensemble. Beginning next summer, the show will evolve into "Marvel's Avengers: Mightiest Friends", and bring additional characters into the fold, including Captain America, Hulk, Black Panther, Black Widow and Thor, according to Disney. For Calandrelli, the role represents another extension of a career dedicated to making space exploration relatable and exciting for the next generation.

In November 2024, Calandrelli became the 100th woman to reach space when she launched aboard Blue Origin's New Shepard rocket on the company's NS-28 suborbital mission. The flight carried her above the Kármán line, the internationally recognized boundary of space, and gave her several minutes of weightlessness before the capsule and its crew returned to Earth.

Calandrelli isn't the first real-life astronaut to lend her voice to the Marvel universe. Former NASA astronaut and the first Black woman in space Mae Jemison guest-starred in Disney's "Marvel's Moon Girl and Devil Dinosaur" in March 2023. Jemison voiced a fictional app called Skipster, created by the show's young superhero and scientific prodigy, Lunella Lafayette. Another space traveler, citizen astronaut Kellie Gerardi, also just announced over the weekend (Oct. 12) her cast credit in the upcoming movie "Hexed", from Disney's Animation Studios.

Viewers can catch the upcoming episode of "Marvel's Iron Man and his Awesome Friends," titled, "The Iron Friends in Space," during its Disney Jr. premiere on Oct. 14 or streaming on Disney+ beginning Oct. 28.

]]> <![CDATA[ NASA's Perseverance Mars rover breaks interplanetary driving record — and it's far from done ]]> In a milestone achievement, NASA's Perseverance Mars rover has broken the record for most miles driven on a world beyond Earth.

On Oct. 11, Perseverance hit 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers) traveled on Mars, breaking the record previously held by NASA's Opportunity rover which went 28.06 miles (45.16 km). It took Oppy 14 years to cover all that ground; Perseverance, by contrast, has been on Mars for just 5.5 years.

The new record is far from the end of Perseverance's journey, however; the mission team thinks the rover could eventually more than double the distance it's already traveled.

"Our original design was only planned to last for [about] 20 kilometers of driving," Mark Maimone, a rover driver at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL) in Southern California, told Space.com.

"We've more than doubled that already … and we're looking really good to go for up to 100 kilometers total," added Maimone, who works as a designated principal in autonomous planetary rover navigation on Perseverance and helped to develop the autonomous driving systems on NASA's previous Mars rovers.

"So we could double what we've done so far," he said. "And we have great expectations that [Perseverance] can continue its mission of exploring and collecting really useful and beneficial samples that will tell us so much more about the history of Mars."

Indeed, Perseverance remains in great shape, mission team members stressed.

"We are very fortunate that all of Perseverance's original capabilities are more or less intact, especially for the science instruments," JPL's Vivian Sun, the mission's deputy project scientist, told Space.com.

Perseverance landed on the floor of Mars' 28-mile-wide (46 km) Jezero Crater in February 2021. It was far from the first robot to traverse the planet's surface; the Perseverance team built on years of experience with the Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity rovers.

Through the triumphs and missteps of these previous craft, NASA learned how to better explore another planet with a rover operated from millions of miles away. Perseverance saw massive improvements made to everything from its specialty wheels to its autonomous driving system and onboard tools and instruments.

This "could not have been done without the previous missions that we've sent to Mars," Sun said.

"Five years later [after landing], we're definitely a very well oiled machine," she added. "There's a lot of technical advancements on Perseverance that are the result of many people, many engineers, working on this new technology year after year for decades now."

And, according to both Sun and Maimone, this teamwork is the real secret behind Perseverance's endurance and success.

"The magic sauce for our operations team is how cohesively we work together," Sun said. The engineers, rover drivers and science team all work together and keep each other's work in mind as they make decisions on everything from driving speed to science targets, she added.

"I'm just super appreciative of all the people that have and still work on the mission. They're really what makes the mission special," Sun said.

What's next for Perseverance

As the team mentioned, Perseverance is nowhere near done on Mars. The rover could keep driving for many more miles on the Red Planet, and the scientists and engineers at NASA have big plans and high hopes for its future.

"We are currently planning to continue down south on the crater rim," Sun said. "There's a whole diversity of different rocks along this crater rim going south that we want to investigate and figure out how it indicates conditions from early Mars."

Jezero is a giant crater created by an impact from an asteroid or comet billions of years ago. Perseverance's work has shown that Jezero hosted a lake for long stretches billions of years ago. Scientists are therefore eager to continue exploring the site, searching for clues about what the planet looked like in the ancient past, and if it could have possibly hosted life.

"There are huge chunks of pre-Jezero crust that were embedded in the stratigraphy or got thrown up by the impact, and they're now incorporated onto the crater rim," Sun said. "These are our chance to probe like really old rocks that don't really exist in any other form on the surface anymore."

As part of Perseverance's next steps south on the crater rim, the team is heading toward an area called "Rainbow Falls."

Sun said that the Rainbow Falls area is thought to have kaolinite, a clay mineral that forms when water interacts with rock. By studying these types of minerals, mission scientists might be able to get a better idea of the conditions on Mars all of those billions of years ago, when water filled Jezero Crater.

"Whenever we are looking at clay minerals, I think the question of habitability and the search for potential biosignatures is always on the table," Sun said. "So that is very much the case when we get to Rainbow Falls, or even when we see kaolinite."

]]> <![CDATA[ Astronaut captures mesmerizing auroras with iPhone from ISS | Space photo of the day for Oct. 13, 2026 ]]>

NASA astronaut Anil Menon captured a gorgeous view of the northern lights dancing over the night side of Earth from the International Space Station on Oct. 10 using an iPhone camera.

What is it?

Menon's photo reveals spectacular pink, purple and red auroras glowing in Earth's upper atmosphere above a sparse dappling of city lights, subtly blurred by the motion of the orbital spacecraft over the course of the exposure.

Bright stars glimmer between the solar panels and outer hulls of the ISS and visiting spacecraft, painted purple by the auroral display. "Flying through is rare and amazing," Menon wrote in a separate aurora video he posted to X on Oct. 10. "You can see the lights on the outside of [the] station reflecting back like Christmas LEDs. It's definitely more immersive."

Why is it amazing?

Menon captured the auroras during a period of heightened geomagnetic activity, after several coronal mass ejections (CMEs) struck Earth's magnetic field, triggering geomagnetic storms ranging from minor (G1) to strong (G3) over the weekend.

During geomagnetic storms, more charged particles are accelerated along Earth's magnetic field lines toward the polar regions, where they collide with gases in the upper atmosphere; they excite them, causing them to release energy as light and producing spectacular auroral displays.

The blue-purple colors seen in Menon's image are largely produced by nitrogen at altitudes of around 60-120 miles (100-200 kilometers) , while the red hue comes from oxygen atoms higher up, typically above 125 miles (200 kilometers).

The photo is particularly impressive because it was captured on an iPhone camera, as opposed to the more traditional Nikon cameras that astronauts sometimes use to capture Earth during their time aboard the ISS.

Smartphone astrophotography has become increasingly popular over recent years, with some models now featuring bespoke modes for capturing the night sky. iPhones were even used by the astronauts of the Artemis 2 mission to document their historic flyby of the moon earlier this year!

Interested in capturing your own images of the night sky using your mobile phone? Then be sure to check out our guide to photographing stars, the moon and the Milky Way with nothing but your smartphone camera.

 <description>V prvním kole senátních voleb bylo zvoleno pět kandidátů, o obsazení zbylých 22 míst rozhodnou voliči v pátek a v sobotu. Podle ústavního právníka Jana Kysely dává většinový volební systém větší šanci uspět lokálně známým osobnostem a ve výsledku vypadá horní komora jinak, než ústavodárci zamýšleli. </description>

<item>
 <title>Udženija: Preferujeme dvojkoalici se Starosty. Třetím by měla být Praha sobě, na Piráty nebyl spoleh</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/volby/udzenija-preferujeme-dvojkoalici-se-starosty-tretim-mela-byt-praha-sobe-na_2610132244_med</link>
 <description>V Praze pokračují povolební vyjednávání. Hnutí Starostů a nezávislých, které v Praze vyhrálo volby, vybírá, s jakými stranami utvoří v hlavním městě koalici. Případná dvojkoalice Starostů s pražským SPOLU (ODS a TOP 09) by měla v pětašedesátičlenném zastupitelstvu těsnou většinu 34 hlasů. „Je to naše preferovaná varianta. Nechceme ale dělat umanutou politiku a jsme otevření dalším jednáním,“ vysvětluje Alexandra Udženija, předsedkyně pražské ODS.</description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/b02dd0842ea40be62232a7a860a7e8cb.jpg?itok=T86PD-US" type="image/jpeg" />

<item>
 <title>Kdo platil letadlo k volbám? Pavel by měl podle Rajchla i koalice zveřejnit náklady na let z Maroka</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/kdo-platil-letadlo-k-volbam-pavel-mel-podle-rajchla-i-koalice-zverejnit-naklady_2610131941_med</link>
 <description>Prezident Petr Pavel by měl podle poslanců vládní koalice zveřejnit náklady na soukromou dovolenou v Maroku kvůli podezření, že ji neplatil jen ze svých peněz. Hlavu státu by k tomu měla vyzvat i Sněmovna, rozhodli poslanci ANO, SPD a Motoristů na návrh Jindřicha Rajchla (SPD/PRO). Výzvu by měla dolní parlamentní komora projednat jako poslední bod nynější schůze. Není ale jisté, zda se k tomu poslanci s ohledem na dvě stovky jiných bodů dostanou.</description>

<item>
 <title>Sokolové chtějí zapsat svoje hnutí na seznam UNESCO. Přehodnotili tedy záměr zapsat tam všesokolský slet</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/sokolove-chteji-zapsat-svoje-hnuti-na-seznam-unesco-prehodnotili-tedy-zamer_2610131906_med</link>
 <description>Sokolové dokončují přípravu návrhu k zapsání České obce sokolské, respektive fenoménu sokolského hnutí, do Seznamu nemateriálního kulturního dědictví České republiky. Následně chtějí podat návrh k zapsání do seznamu nehmotného dědictví UNESCO. Vyplývá to z odpovědí mluvčí Sokolu Johany Homolové. Obec chtěla původně na seznam nehmotného dědictví UNESCO zapsat všesokolský slet, záměr přehodnotila po jednání s ministerstvem kultury.</description>

 <description>V obvodě 72 Ostrava-město se o mandát uchází senátor, lékař a vysokoškolský pedagog Ondřej Šimetka (za ODS) a starostka Ostravy-Poruby a náměstkyně primátora Lucie Baránková Vilamová (ANO). Šimetka v prvním kole získal 46,74 procenta hlasů, Baránková Vilamová skončila druhá se ziskem 30,61 procenta. Poslechněte si jejich debatu.</description>

 <description>V senátním obvodě číslo 60 obhajuje mandát Zdeněk Papoušek (ODS), který do druhého kola voleb postoupil z prvního místa s podporou 42,1 procenta. Jeho vyzyvatelem je Karel Zitterbart (STAN), který oslovil v prvním kole 24,4 procenta voličů. Poslechněte si jejich debatu.</description>

<item>
 <title>‚Asi nejzásadnější chyba letošních voleb.‘ Strany sbírají podklady k soudu, chtějí přepočítat hlasy</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/asi-nejzasadnejsi-chyba-letosnich-voleb-strany-sbiraji-podklady-k-soudu-chteji_2610131804_ako</link>
 <description>Komunální volby oficiálně skončily, přesto by se výsledky ještě někde mohly změnit. Některé strany totiž chtějí podat návrh na přezkum ke krajským soudům. Upozorňují na údajné chyby při sčítání hlasů. Jako třeba v Karviné nebo Praze 10, kde se může hrát dokonce o dva mandáty. Lhůta pro podání návrhu začne běžet ve středu a strany na to budou mít deset dnů.</description>

</item>
<item>
 <title>Krajský soud v Brně uložil nepravomocný trest odnětí svobody rodičům zemřelé holčičky, zanedbali péči</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-domov/krajsky-soud-v-brne-ulozil-nepravomocny-trest-odneti-svobody-rodicum-zemrele_2610131557_tez</link>
 <description>Krajský soud v Brně uložil v úterý 13. října nepravomocný trest odnětí svody rodičům zemřelé holčičky. Matka má ve vězení strávit osm let, otec šest. Zdravotní problémy miminka rodiče neřešily několik dní a záchrannou službu přivolali až v momentě, kdy chrčelo a modralo. Lékaři už holčičce nedokázali pomoci. </description>
 <enclosure url="https://www.irozhlas.cz/sites/default/files/styles/zpravy_maly_nahled/public/images/916e1f519319f878f76a1073397a5d3f.jpg?itok=rU9vWqxk" type="image/jpeg" />
 <pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 17:39:00 +0200</pubDate>
</item>

   <title>Konec levných nákupů z Asie? EU zavádí od listopadu poplatek za každou zásilku</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ekonomika/evropa-cesko-posta-nove-poplatky-za-baliky-z-asie/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ekonomika</link>
   <description>Nakupování na oblíbených online tržištích od listopadu znovu podraží. Evropská unie totiž zpřísňuje pravidla pro dovoz ze třetích zemí. Za každý balíček mířící z Asie a dalších zemí mimo Evropu si zákazníci připlatí desítky korun. Celní úřady jsou totiž zahlceny miliardami balíků ročně, hlavně z Číny. Odborníci ale varují, že finanční opatření sama o sobě neřeší hlavní problém v podobě kontroly možného nebezpečného zboží. </description>
   <pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 19:00:00 +0200</pubDate>

  <item>
   <title>Pepřový sprej v kabelce. Víte, jak ho použít? V České Lípě proběhne kurz</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/volny-cas/peprovy-sprej-v-kabelce-vite-jak-ho-pouzit-v-ceske-lipe-probehne-kurz/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=volny-cas</link>
   <description>Pepřový sprej dnes nosí řada žen v kabelce nebo batohu. Často jako pojistku pro případ, že by se někdy dostaly do nepříjemné situace. Jenže mít ho u sebe ještě neznamená umět ho použít. Pomoci může chystaný kurz, který proběhne v České Lípě 22. října.</description>

   <title>Nezaměstnanost v Libereckém kraji v září klesla. Mladých bez práce přibylo</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/nezamestnanost-v-libereckem-kraji-v-zari-klesla-mladych-bez-prace-pribylo/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Nezaměstnanost v Libereckém kraji se v září mírně snížila. Podíl nezaměstnaných klesl na 5,6 procenta a z evidence úřadu práce odešlo více lidí, než kolik jich nově přibylo. Ve srovnání s loňským zářím je však v regionu stále o 1 259 nezaměstnaných více. Výrazně narostl také počet mladých lidí, kteří po prázdninách hledají práci.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Tejc změní rozvodovou novelu. Dítě má více chránit před násilným rodičem</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/cesko-zmena-rozvodova-novela-dite-bude-vic-chranit-pred-nasilnym-rodicem/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=cesko</link>
   <description>Vláda 12. října schválila návrh ministerstva spravedlnosti, který upravuje sporné části rozvodové novely schválené minulou vládou a platné od 1. ledna 2026. Změny reagují na výhrady odborníků i zkušenosti soudů a mají lépe chránit děti, zejména v případech domácího násilí, vyhrocených sporů mezi rodiči nebo jiných situací, kdy může být ohrožena bezpečnost dětí. Novela zároveň přináší jasnější pravidla pro rozhodování soudů a klade větší důraz na nejlepší zájem dítěte.</description>
   <pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:00:00 +0200</pubDate>
   <guid>https://www.denik.cz/cesko/cesko-zmena-rozvodova-novela-dite-bude-vic-chranit-pred-nasilnym-rodicem/</guid>

   <media:content url="https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/images/api/image/1366x768/1b1/1b164ef3-4709-493e-8e10-cf6d647c5f03.jpeg" medium="image" height="768" width="1366">
    <media:description>Změny v rodičovské novele mají více posílit práva dítěte, jeho bezpečnost a jeho přání.</media:description>

    <item>
      <title>Mzda strachu v Hormuzu: 100 tisíc dolarů za měsíc. Proč je drahá ropa</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ropa-hormuzem-stale-proudi-benzin-presto-zdrazuje-vinu-nese-draha-doprava.A261013_172657_zahranicni_ichuc#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>V Hormuzu prožívají kapitáni tankerů zlaté časy, tedy pokud je něco netrefí. Je to jejich Klondike. Nyní může kapitán tankeru počítat s tím, že dostane základní mzdu sto tisíc dolarů měsíčně. Než válka začala, viděl na výplatní pásce něco mezi dvaceti až padesáti tisíci. Ale ta hlavní zlatá žíla je pro něj ještě někde jinde. Jakmile propluje Hormuzem ven, dostane prémii 50 000 dolarů. A když projede zase zpátky, dalších 50 000 dolarů.</description>
      <pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 22:00:00 GMT</pubDate>
      <category domain="https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni">Zprávy - Zahraničí</category>
      <comments>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ropa-hormuzem-stale-proudi-benzin-presto-zdrazuje-vinu-nese-draha-doprava.A261013_172657_zahranicni_ichuc/diskuse</comments>
      <guid isPermaLink="false">A261013_172657_zahranicni_ichuc</guid>
      <media:content url="https://1gr.cz/fotky/idnes/26/102/cl6/IHA8fec07b9b5_profimedia_1081933877.jpg" type="image/jpeg" />
      <media:description>Průjezd Hormuzem není snadný, jen od 20. září se tam  stalo sedmadvacet útoků a incidentů, kapitáni ale mají majlant.</media:description>
      <media:credit>Profimedia.cz</media:credit>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Vraždila ve škole, teď je venku z detence. Klepu se a mám vztek, říká otec oběti</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/jihlava/zpravy/vrazedkyne-barbora-orlova-petr-vejvoda-otec-zdar-nad-sazavou.A261013_164442_jihlava-zpravy_evs#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Přesně před dvanácti lety přišel Kamil Vejvoda o svého jediného syna Petra. Tehdy šestnáctiletý student obchodní akademie ve Žďáru nad Sázavou 14. října 2014 bránil spolužačku a sám při tom přišel o život. Ubodala ho psychicky vyšinutá útočnice Barbora Orlová, která později skončila v zabezpečovací detenci. Jenže tu teď opustila.

</description>

    <item>
      <title>Mladým se hledá první práce čím dál hůř. Nejtěžší to mají ti bez vzdělání a praxe</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/ekonomika/domaci/mladym-se-hleda-prvni-prace-cim-dal-hur-nejtezsi-to-maji-ti-bez-vzdelani-a-praxe.A261013_145759_ekonomika_kris#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Je to klasická patová situace. Mladý člověk nemůže najít práci, protože nemá praxi. Tu ale nemůže získat, protože ho bez zkušeností nikdo nechce zaměstnat. Přestože se nezaměstnanost v Česku stále drží na jedné z nejnižších úrovní v Evropě, mladí lidé mají vstup na pracovní trh stále složitější.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Vůdce gangu odsoudili za vraždu rappera Shakura. Ve vězení si odsedí desítky let</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/vrazda-tupac-odsouzeni-40-let-vezeni-dozivoti.A261013_215131_zahranicni_balu#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Bývalý vůdce pouličního gangu Duane „Keffe D“ Davis byl odsouzen ke 40 letům až doživotí za zosnování vraždy rappera Tupaca Shakura, kterého v roce 1996 zastřelili v Las Vegas. O podmínečné propuštění bude moci 63letý Davis požádat nejdříve po odpykání 40 let, podle žalobců tak pravděpodobně stráví zbytek života ve vězení. Porota ho v srpnu uznala vinným z vraždy prvního stupně se střelnou zbraní.</description>

<item>
<title>Čeští vědci vyvíjejí s Lockheed Martin umělou inteligenci, která z řeči pozná přetíženého pilota</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesti-vedci-vyvijeji-s-lockheed-martin-umelou-inteligenci-ktera-z-reci-pozna-pretizeneho-pilota/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Če&#353;tí vědci z Fakulty informačních technologií VUT v Brně spolupracují s americkým gigantem Lockheed Martin na vývoji umělé inteligence, která má rozpoznat, kdy je vojenský pilot pod nebezpečným tlakem. Systém analyzuje změny v jeho hlase a porovnává je s údaji o fyzickém stavu získanými z dal&#353;ích senzorů. Cílem je odhalit kognitivní přetížení dřív, než takový stav ohrozí pilota nebo letadlo.</description>

<description>Český operátor O2 se chystá na akvizici na tuzemském trhu. Chce převzít IT společnost Ness Czech, kterou ovládá velký americký fond KKR. Ten má ve správě aktiva za zhruba 760 miliard dolarů.</description>

<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/ceske-radiokomunikace-reorganizuji-cenny-majetek-klicovy-byznys-prechazi-na-jine-firmy/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>České Radiokomunikace (CRA) od leto&#353;ního listopadu reorganizují svůj stále rostoucí a důležitěj&#353;í byznys s datovými centry, cloudem a provozem serverů. Z CRA budou prvního listopadu vyčleněna aktiva do dvou nástupnických firem, kterými budou Datové centrum Lužice a Cloud4com. CRA jsou v obou jediným akcionářem.</description>

 <description>Někdejší vůdce gangu Duane „Keffe D“ Davis byl za zosnování vraždy 25letého rapera Tupaca Shakura v roce 1996 nyní odsouzen ke 40 letům až doživotí za mřížemi, píše agentura AP. O podmínečné propuštění bude 63letý Davis moci požádat nejdříve za 40 let, pravděpodobně tak stráví zbytek života ve vězení. Porota v srpnu Davise shledala vinným z vraždy smrtící zbraní se záměrem propagovat, upevnit pozici či pomoci Shakurovou smrtí kriminálnímu gangu.</description>

 <description>Americká velvyslankyně v Řecku Kimberly Guilfoyleová končí ve funkci. Diplomatka to oznámila na síti X krátce poté, co mluvčí Bílého domu Katie Zachariaová na tiskové konferenci oznámila, že Guilfoyleová byla požádána, aby rezignovala. Prezident Donald Trump už v pondělí uváděl, že uvažuje o propuštění diplomatky, a vyjádřil znepokojení nad zprávami, že velvyslankyně využila své pozice a vazeb na Trumpovu rodinu, aby získala peníze od dárce. </description>

 <description>Počet potvrzených případů eboly v Kongu vzrostl na 9066, včetně 4381 úmrtí. Podle agentury Reuters to vyplývá z v úterý zveřejněných údajů konžského institutu veřejného zdraví. Nynější epidemie, která byla vyhlášena v provincii Ituri v polovině května, svým rozsahem i počtem obětí přesahuje epidemii, která zemi zasáhla v letech 2018 až 2020. </description>

 <description>Americký prezident Donald Trump se dál ostře vymezuje proti ukrajinskému prezidentovi Zelenskému. Nově prohlásil, že ruský prezident Vladimir Putin má větší zájem dohodnout se než hlava ukrajinského státu. „Republikánské straně špatně vychází prognózy. Jedním z těch důvodů je vysoká cena ropy. A přeci Trump nepřizná: já jsem to zkazil tím, že jsem zaútočil na Írán,“ říká Jakub Lepš, amerikanista, který kandidoval v komunálních volbách (TOP 09).</description>

 <description>Maďarští poslanci v úterý odhlasovali zrušení právních ustanovení proti LGBT+ komunitě. Pro se vyslovilo 139 z nich, 59 hlasovalo proti, informovala agentura AFP.  <description>„Za poslední tři měsíce z našich kohoutků netekla ani kapka,“ říká obyvatelka ostrova Batam v Indonésii. Nedávno tu totiž vznikla dvě datová centra a další ještě přibydou – úřady jich celkem schválily deset. Už teď ale mají místní problém s nedostatkem pitné vody. Za vinu to dávají právě vybudovaným centrům. Ta totiž denně v průměru spotřebují stejné množství vody jako 1000 amerických domácností.</description>

<title>Čeští vědci vyvíjejí s Lockheed Martin umělou inteligenci, která z řeči pozná přetíženého pilota</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesti-vedci-vyvijeji-s-lockheed-martin-umelou-inteligenci-ktera-z-reci-pozna-pretizeneho-pilota/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Če&#353;tí vědci z Fakulty informačních technologií VUT v Brně spolupracují s americkým gigantem Lockheed Martin na vývoji umělé inteligence, která má rozpoznat, kdy je vojenský pilot pod nebezpečným tlakem. Systém analyzuje změny v jeho hlase a porovnává je s údaji o fyzickém stavu získanými z dal&#353;ích senzorů. Cílem je odhalit kognitivní přetížení dřív, než takový stav ohrozí pilota nebo letadlo.</description>

<description>Český operátor O2 se chystá na akvizici na tuzemském trhu. Chce převzít IT společnost Ness Czech, kterou ovládá velký americký fond KKR. Ten má ve správě aktiva za zhruba 760 miliard dolarů.</description>

Kudy z nudy – Žebříčky: Liberecký kraj Žebříčky RSS Feed <![CDATA[Šťastné a křišťálové – Vánoce naruby]]>

Přijďte prožít advent do libereckého Paláce Liebieg, kde se letos potkají tradice, kreativita a vánoční atmosféra Křišťálového údolí. Čeká vás jedinečná výstava, která vás zavede do světa fantazie, kde nic není takové, jak se na první pohled zdá.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 15:54:49 GMT <![CDATA[Židovská modlitebna a synagoga Liberec]]>

Novodobá liberecká synagoga je součástí Krajské vědecké knihovny, známé jako Stavba smíření. Otevřena byla roku 2000 na místě synagogy vypálené nacisty. Trojúhelníkový půdorys připomíná část Davidovy hvězdy a interiér uchovává památky původního svatostánku.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:36:28 GMT <![CDATA[Kostel sv. Vojtěcha v Liberci]]>

Kostel sv. Vojtěcha v libereckém Ostašově stojí na místě dřevěné kaple vybudované z odškodnění za sedmiletou válku. Zděná stavba vznikla v letech 1832–1833. Díky péči Spolku přátel Ostašova dnes ožívá koncerty a dalšími kulturními akcemi.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:29:30 GMT <![CDATA[Kostel sv. Jana Křtitele v Liberci]]>

Barokní kostel sv. Jana Křtitele v liberecké Rochlici stojí na místě někdejšího dřevěného evangelického kostela. Zaujme dochovaným historickým vybavením, hlavním oltářem s obrazem patrona chrámu, vyřezávanou kazatelnou a varhanami z roku 1887.

]]> Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:23:32 GMT

<rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>Konec omezení v Hodkovicích. Most přes silnici 35 se otevře</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902885-konec-omezeni-hodkovicich-most-pres-silnici-35-se-otevre.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902885-konec-omezeni-hodkovicich-most-pres-silnici-35-se-otevre.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 20:01:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Už ve čtvrtek se otevře most přes silnici I/35 v Hodkovicích, po půl roce tak skončí dopravní omezení v okolí mostu. Výměna mostu ŘSD přišla na 72 milionů korun.</description></item><item><title>Co se dělo minulý týden? Prověřte své znalosti v křížovce</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kvizy/902855-co-se-delo-minuly-tyden-proverte-sve-znalosti-v-krizovce.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/kvizy/902855-co-se-delo-minuly-tyden-proverte-sve-znalosti-v-krizovce.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 18:15:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Kvízy</category><description>Pojďte se pobavit a připomenout si, o čem Liberecká Drbna psala minulý týden. Přinášíme novou várku křižovek.</description></item><item><title>Darujte nevyužité vánoční ozdoby, pomůžete onkologicky nemocným v kraji</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902835-darujte-nevyuzite-vanocni-ozdoby-pomuzete-onkologicky-nemocnym-v-kraji.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902835-darujte-nevyuzite-vanocni-ozdoby-pomuzete-onkologicky-nemocnym-v-kraji.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 16:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Centrum Amelie Liberec vyhlašuje tradiční sbírku vánočních dekorací. Nepotřebné ozdoby, které doma jen leží, můžete do 30. listopadu věnovat na sběrných místech. Jejich následný prodej pomůže financovat bezplatnou psychosociální péči pro onkologicky nemocné a jejich rodiny.</description></item><item><title>Tragická nehoda v Jablonci. Couvající dodávka srazila muže, zemřel</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/902918-tragicka-nehoda-v-jablonci-couvajici-dodavka-srazila-muze-zemrel.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/902918-tragicka-nehoda-v-jablonci-couvajici-dodavka-srazila-muze-zemrel.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 14:12:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Tragická dopravní nehoda se dnes dopoledne stala v Jablonci nad Nisou v Pražské ulici. Řidič kurýrní dodávky při couvání přehlédl muže, který vstoupil do vozovky zpoza nákladního auta. Chodec přes veškerou snahu záchranářů na místě svému zranění podlehl.</description></item><item><title>Areál bývalého sanatoria v Machníně ožil. Začala stavba Alzheimer centra</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902894-areal-byvaleho-sanatoria-v-machnine-ozil-zacala-stavba-alzheimer-centra.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902894-areal-byvaleho-sanatoria-v-machnine-ozil-zacala-stavba-alzheimer-centra.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 13:21:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Dlouhé roky areál bývalého očního sanatoria v libereckém Machníně chátral. Město jej vykoupilo od soukromého majitele, scelilo pozemky a dlouho se jej opět prodat snažilo. To se nakonec podařilo a developer Dolcevita zde vybuduje Alzheimer centrum a v další etapě domov pro seniory.</description></item><item><title>V Jablonci po volbách bez výraznější změny. Koalice pokračuje, ANO je v opozici</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/902889-v-jablonci-po-volbach-bez-vyraznejsi-zmeny-koalice-pokracuje-ano-je-v-opozici.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/902889-v-jablonci-po-volbach-bez-vyraznejsi-zmeny-koalice-pokracuje-ano-je-v-opozici.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Jablonec nad Nisou povede v příštích čtyřech letech koalice složená ze zástupců Starostů pro Liberecký kraj, ODS, Společně pro Jablonec a Pirátů a nezávislých. Primátorem zůstane Miloš Vele z ODS. Vítěz voleb ANO zůstává v opozici.</description></item><item><title>Vesecký areál zaplavily stovky školáků. Konal se okresní přebor v přespolním běhu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/sport/902857-vesecky-areal-zaplavily-stovky-skolaku-konal-se-okresni-prebor-v-prespolnim-behu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/sport/902857-vesecky-areal-zaplavily-stovky-skolaku-konal-se-okresni-prebor-v-prespolnim-behu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:56:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Sport</category><description>Téměř čtyři stovky mladých sportovců ze základních a středních škol Liberecka změřily síly na tradičním Okresním kole v přespolním běhu. Sportovní areál ve Vesci zažil v úterý 6. října skvělou atmosféru, ve které si běžci sáhli na dno sil a bojovali o postup do krajského finále.</description></item><item><title>Kraj chce příští rok začít stavět novou zdravotnickou školu v Liberci</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/vzdelani/902834-kraj-chce-pristi-rok-zacit-stavet-novou-zdravotnickou-skolu-v-liberci.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/vzdelani/902834-kraj-chce-pristi-rok-zacit-stavet-novou-zdravotnickou-skolu-v-liberci.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:53:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Vzdělání</category><description>Liberecký kraj chce příští rok zahájit stavbu nové budovy pro střední zdravotnickou školu v Liberci, počítá s tím v rozpočtovém výhledu. Po centru urgentní medicíny to bude druhý nejdražší projekt kraje, náklady projektanti odhadují na 1,2 miliardy korun.</description></item><item><title>Výhled, na který se čekalo sedmdesát let: Rozhledna na Javorníku otevře 28. října</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902833-vyhled-na-ktery-se-cekalo-sedmdesat-let-rozhledna-na-javorniku-otevre-28-rijna.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/902833-vyhled-na-ktery-se-cekalo-sedmdesat-let-rozhledna-na-javorniku-otevre-28-rijna.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 13 Oct 2026 06:30:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Po více než sedmdesáti letech se návštěvníkům Javorníku znovu otevírá výhled do kraje, a to díky nové rozhledně u hotelu Obří sud, která rozšířila nabídku areálu Adventure Park Liberec. Slavnostně bude otevřena ve středu 28. října v 10 hodin. Už teď ale funguje ve zkušebním provozu a je přístupná.</description></item><item><title>Dvě nedělní nehody na Jablonecku: Zatáčky vynesly řidiče do patníku i protisměru</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902804-dve-nedelni-nehody-na-jablonecku-zatacky-vynesly-ridice-do-patniku-i-protismeru.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/902804-dve-nedelni-nehody-na-jablonecku-zatacky-vynesly-ridice-do-patniku-i-protismeru.html</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 19:28:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Neděle na Jablonecku se neobešla bez nehod na silnicích. Dva řidiči doplatili na neopatrnost v levotočivých zatáčkách – jeden skončil v protisměru a způsobil zranění druhého šoféra, další se svým vozem narazil čelně do kamenného patníku. Alkohol byl u obou vyloučen.</description></item></channel></rss>
